--- order: 3 unit: data introduces: [vue-on, vue-model] assumes: [input-value] title: "Events and inputs" summary: "Run a function of your own when something is clicked, join a box to data with v-model, and change a ref's .value in the script." language: html voice: { name: af_heart, speed: 1.1 } app: command: node "$REPO_ROOT/tools/serve.mjs" "$REPO_ROOT/dist/_playground-dom" 8131 url: http://127.0.0.1:8131/index.html ready: HTML and JavaScript code layout: full pacing: keyDelayMs: 6 explainPicture: page.html#run explainClip: query: {code: "@page.html#explain-start", zoom: 1.4} caption: "A function in setup changes the data; in the script, the value is in .value" clip: - caption: "A score, made with ref." - wait: 400 - caption: {text: "A function in setup adds a point to score.value.", say: "A function in setup adds a point to score dot value."} - type: {into: "HTML and JavaScript code", text: " function addPoint() {\n score.value++;\n }\n", after: "const score = ref(0);\n"} - type: {into: "HTML and JavaScript code", text: ", addPoint", after: "return { score"} - caption: "The button runs the function." - type: {into: "HTML and JavaScript code", text: " \n", after: "

\n"} - click: "Run ▶" - expect: {selector: "#status", contains: "Running"} - wait: 600 - click: {selector: "button", preview: true} - click: {selector: "button", preview: true} - expect: {selector: "p", contains: "Score: 2", preview: true} - caption: "Page: score. Script: score.value." - wait: 300 hook: "Type in a box, press Add, and the list updates. Vue joins the event and the data for you." --- Two new pieces join the page to the data. **Events:** `@click="addPlayer"` runs a function when the button is clicked. The function lives in `setup` and is returned like the data: ```js function addPlayer() { players.value.push(newName.value); newName.value = ""; } return { players, newName, addPlayer }; ``` **Inputs:** `v-model="newName"` joins a box to a ref, both ways: typing changes the data, and changing the data changes the box. No `.value` of the box and no `"input"` event, as in the DOM course. **The hard part:** on the page you write `newName`; in the script you write `newName.value`. A ref is a box, and in the script you open it yourself. ## Predict ```step stage: predict code: page.html#predict insight: "Students from the DOM course expect to need an input event; seeing the paragraph follow each letter shows that v-model joins box and data." check: type: predict q: "You clear the box and type Kai. What does the paragraph show while you type?" options: ["It changes with every letter, ending Hello, Kai!", "Hello, friend! until you press Enter", "Hello, friend! all along: nothing listens to the box", "Hello, {{ name }}!"] actual: "It changes with every letter. v-model puts what you type into name straight away, and {{ name }} shows it." ``` There is no event and no `.value` here, only `v-model`. ## Run ```step stage: run code: page.html#run try: { playground: dom, starter: "page.html#run", height: 440 } check: { type: reflect, text: "I added two names and saw the box empty itself after each one." } ``` Press **Run**, type a name and press **Add**. Then press Add with the box empty: nothing happens, because of the `if`. ## Investigate ```step stage: investigate code: page.html#run insight: "v-model joins box and data both ways; @click runs a returned function; in the script a ref's value is in .value." tasks: - check: type: match q: "Match each part with what it does." pairs: - ["v-model=\"newName\"", "joins the box and newName, both ways"] - ["@click=\"addPlayer\"", "runs addPlayer when the button is clicked"] - ["players.value.push(newName.value);", "adds the typed name to the list"] - ["newName.value = \"\";", "empties the data, and so the box"] - ["return { players, newName, addPlayer };", "lets the page use the data and the function"] explain: "Setting newName.value to empty text also empties the box: v-model works in both directions." - check: type: question q: "Why does the function write newName.value, but the page writes newName?" options: ["The page opens refs for you; in the script you open them yourself with .value", "They are two different variables", ".value is only for inputs", "It is a mistake: both should be the same"] answer: 0 explain: "newName is a ref, a box Vue watches. The page unwraps it for you; the script reaches the value inside with .value." - check: type: bug code: page.html#bug text: "Clicking Add a point shows a red error, and the score stays at 0. Click the line that is wrong." answer: 13 fault: runtime misconception: vue-value-in-script explain: "score is a ref, made with const. score++ tries to change the box itself. The number is score.value, so write score.value++." ``` ### Which part does what? Box, button and function. ### Two ways to write it The page and the script. ### Spot the bug The score will not change. ## Modify ```step stage: modify insight: "A new function is written in setup, returned, and named in @click; a new box is one v-model on a new ref." try: { playground: dom, starter: "page.html#run", height: 440 } tasks: - hint: - "A function in setup, returned, and a button that names it." - "`function reset() { players.value = [\"Ada\", \"Sam\"]; newName.value = \"\"; }` then add reset to the return, and ``." expected: page.html#sol-reset check: { type: code, text: "Add a Reset button that puts the list back to Ada and Sam.", rules: { contains: ["function reset", "@click=\"reset\""] } } - hint: - "A new box needs a new ref, returned, and v-model on the box." - "`const club = ref(\"Chess\");`, club in the return, ``, and `{{ club }}` in the heading." expected: page.html#sol-club check: { type: code, text: "Add a box for the club's name, and show it in the heading.", rules: { contains: ["v-model=\"club\"", "{{ club }}"] } } ``` ### Reset A function of your own. ### The club's name A second box. ## Make: a badge maker ```step stage: make insight: "Goals only: boxes joined with v-model, the result shown with {{ }}, and a button that runs a function which changes .value." try: { playground: dom, starter: "page.html#make", height: 440 } check: { type: code, text: "Make boxes with v-model, show them on a badge, and add a button that runs a function of your own.", rules: { contains: ["v-model", "function", "@click"] } } ``` Make a **name badge**: boxes for a name and a role joined with `v-model`, the badge shown with `{{ }}` in a bordered box, and a button that runs a function (make the name shout in capitals with `toUpperCase()`, or swap the two). ## Where this leads ```step stage: info check: type: question q: "Your page should show how many players there are, and say Team full at 5. Where should the count come from?" options: ["Worked out from the list, so it is always right", "A second ref you change by hand in every function", "Counted by the page", "Typed in a box"] answer: 0 explain: "A value worked out from other data should be worked out again whenever that data changes. Next: computed." ``` Next: **values worked out from data**, with `computed`. ```teacher summary: Students predict that v-model follows each letter, add names with a function, match the parts, find score++ on a ref, add a Reset function and a second box, and make a badge maker. time: 55 timing: Predict and Run 10 min · Investigate 15 min · Modify 15 min · Make 15 min goals: - I can run a function of my own when a button is clicked. - I can join a box to data with v-model. - I can change a ref in the script with .value. before: > Read the unit primer first. Two new pieces. `@click="addPlayer"` names a function to run on a click; the function is written in `setup` and returned with the data. `v-model="newName"` joins a box to a ref both ways: typing changes the ref, and setting the ref (to empty text, say) changes the box. Compare the DOM course, where students read `box.value` and listened for the `"input"` event themselves. **The hard part of the whole course:** a ref is a box. On the page Vue opens it for you (`{{ score }}`, `@click="score++"`); in the script you open it yourself (`score.value++`). Writing `score++` in a function gives a red error, "Assignment to constant variable", because the ref was made with `const`. The playground's hint names `.value` for this case. Expect it all lesson; it is also the planted bug. running: - "Predict: ask what DOM-course students would have needed (an input event and box.value)." - "Run: press Add with an empty box and ask which line stops it." - "Investigate: before the bug, ask students to underline every .value in the script and none on the page." - "Modify: a new function is three edits: write it, return it, name it in @click." - "Make: ask which ref each box changes, and what the button's function changes." struggle: Students mix up when to write .value. Ask "are you on the page or in the script?" every time, and let them answer before they type. stuck: - see: "A red error: Assignment to constant variable." ask: Is that a ref, changed in the script? fix: "Change its .value: score.value++." - see: Clicking does nothing; the console warns a property is not defined. ask: Is the function in the return? fix: return { players, newName, addPlayer, reset }; - see: The box and the paragraph do not match. ask: Does v-model name the same ref the paragraph shows? fix: Use the same name in v-model and in {{ }}. stretch: 'Add when Enter is pressed: @keyup.enter="addPlayer" on the box. Remove a player when their name is clicked (pass the name to a function).' support: Give the Reset function written out; students return it and add the button. leads: "Next lesson: computed values, worked out from data and kept up to date. Class idea: find an Add button on a real site and say which data it changes." exit: q: In a Vue function, how do you add 1 to a ref called score, and why is it different on the page? a: score.value++; the page unwraps refs for you, but the script reaches the value inside with .value. explain: | 1. A score on the page, made with `ref`. 2. A function in `setup` adds a point. 3. In the script, the number is in `score.value`. 4. The button runs the function when it is clicked: `@click="addPoint"`. 5. On the page you write `score`; in the script, `score.value`. solutions: step-4#t1: page.html#sol-reset step-4#t2: page.html#sol-club step-5: page.html#sol-make sources: - title: "Vue.js: Event handling" url: https://vuejs.org/guide/essentials/event-handling.html checked: 2026-10-12 - title: "Vue.js: Form input bindings (v-model)" url: https://vuejs.org/guide/essentials/forms.html checked: 2026-10-12 ```
